headline: West Indies' Alzarri Holder retires from ODIs
summary: The fast bowler has stepped away from the 50-over format of the game.
details: West Indies fast bowler Alzarri Holder has announced his retirement from One Day International (ODI) cricket.
The decision was confirmed by West Indies captain Sammy Joseph, who shared the news of the the bowler's departure from the format.
Holder's retirement marks the end of his career in the 50-over game for the West Indies team.
The team will now look to integrate new bowling options as they prepare for upcoming international fixtures.
caption:
A major blow to the West Indies bowling attack. Alzarri Holder is officially out of ODIs.

West Indies fast bowler Alzarri Holder has announced his retirement from One Day International (ODI) cricket.

The decision was confirmed by West Indies captain Sammy Joseph, who shared the news of the the bowler's departure from the format.

Holder's retirement marks the end of his career in the 50-over game for the West Indies team.

The team will now look to integrate new bowling options as they prepare for upcoming international fixtures.

headline_marked: Train services [[resume on Chittagong–Cox's Bazar route]] after flood disruptions
headline: Train services resume on Chittagong–Cox's Bazar route after flood disruptions
summary: Rail services have returned to normal on the route connecting Chittagong and Cox's Bazar following previous interruptions caused by floods.
details: Train services on the Chittagong–Cox's Bazar route have returned to normal after being disrupted by recent floods.
The restoration of services allows passengers to travel between the major port city and the popular tourist destination of Cox's Bazar.
The disruptions were caused by floodwaters that affected the railway tracks and infrastructure in the region.
Railway authorities have ensured the tracks are safe for operation as services resume their regular schedules.
caption:
Trains are back on track! 🚂

Train services on the Chittagong–Cox's Bazar route have returned to normal after being disrupted by recent floods.

The restoration of services allows passengers to travel between the major port city and the popular tourist destination of Cox's Bazar.

The disruptions were caused by floodwaters that affected the railway tracks and infrastructure in the region.

Railway authorities have ensured the tracks are safe for operation as services resume their regular schedules.
